parsed_output.analysis: The specification requires a simple HumanDrivingMode state, a composite AutonomousMode with sub-states, start in HumanDrivingMode on power on, move to AutonomousMode when front_distance > 10, return to HumanDrivingMode on human steering cmd + brake pressed only when in the autonomous final sub-state, and go to a final state on power off. The PlantUML model implements the start, the front_distance guard and the composite structure, but it adds an extra return transition from the operational sub-state and it routes Power Off to the UML final terminator [*] rather than to a named final state.

issues.issue: Human steering cmd / brake pressed return allowed from AutoOperationalState
issues.reason: Specification says transit to human driving mode when receive human steering cmd, brake pressed, in (auto final). The model permits the same guard from AutoOperationalState, i.e. from a non-final autonomous sub-state, which is not specified.
issues.where: AutoOperationalState -> HumanDrivingMode : human steering cmd, brake pressed

issues.issue: Power Off targets termination [*] instead of a final state
issues.reason: Specification states ‘when power off, it will transit to final state’. The model uses the UML terminator [*] for power off from both HumanDrivingMode and AutonomousMode. HumanDrivingMode has no final sub-state and AutonomousMode’s power-off exit bypasses the named AutoFinalState: Final State that exists inside the composite.
issues.where: HumanDrivingMode -> [*] : Power Off and AutonomousMode -> [*] : Power Off

issues.issue: Return transition from AutoFinalState is present but the specification’s scope of the human-intervention return is ambiguous
issues.reason: The model correctly provides a human-intervention return from AutoFinalState, matching the spec’s ‘in (auto final)’ intent, however because the model also provides the same return from AutoOperationalState the overall behavior is broader than specified.
issues.where: AutoFinalState -> HumanDrivingMode : human steering cmd, brake pressed

system_prompt:
You are an experienced control-systems engineer reviewing a state machine model against the natural-language specification it was built from.

You are given two things, both complete and unmodified:
  1. The natural-language specification.
  2. A state machine model written in PlantUML.

Your task: identify the places where the model does not conform to the specification. Read the specification in full first, then read the model in full, then report what you find.

Report as many or as few issues as you actually find, and organize them however you judge best. For each issue, state what the non-conformance is, which part of the model it concerns, and why you consider it a non-conformance.

Write your findings in en-US. Return only the requested structured response.
user_prompt:
## Natural-language specification

1 The human driving mode is represented by a simple state. 2 The autonomous mode has sub-states and is represented by a sub machine state. 3. when power on, the system turn into human driving mode 4when front_distance > 10, auto transport to autonomous state 4. transit to human driving mode when receive human steering cmd, brake pressed, in (auto final) 5 when power off, it will transit to final state

## State machine model (PlantUML)

@startuml
[*] -> HumanDrivingMode
HumanDrivingMode: Human Driving Mode
HumanDrivingMode -> AutonomousMode: front_distance > 10
AutonomousMode: Autonomous Mode
state AutonomousMode {
[*] -> AutoInitialState
AutoInitialState: Initial State
AutoInitialState -> AutoOperationalState: Signal Transmission Succeeds
AutoOperationalState: Operational State
AutoOperationalState -> AutoFinalState: Mission Completed
AutoFinalState: Final State
AutoOperationalState -> HumanDrivingMode: human steering cmd, brake pressed
AutoFinalState -> HumanDrivingMode: human steering cmd, brake pressed
}
HumanDrivingMode -> [*]: Power Off
AutonomousMode -> [*]: Power Off
@enduml
